21323-what-the-church-means-to-me-a-fran:
Wilfred T. Grenfell, the doctor and missionary famous for his medical mission in Labrador, published this frank confession in 1911. The church, he says, means all who are forwarding God's kingdom on earth, consciously or not. Any body that claims the title for itself alone, he calls ridiculous.

Through the church, Grenfell writes, came his spiritual sight, strength in weakness, comfort in trial, and help in need. He argues that how people organise worship gives no one a right to exclude others doing Christ's work another way. It is a short, warm statement from a practical Christian who spent his life running hospitals, ships, and schools in the North.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-johann-gabrie:
Johann Gabriel Seidl, Austrian poet and author of the present national hymn's text, was born at Vienna in 1804 and died there in 1875. Of Swiss stock, son of an able lawyer and a capable housewife, he passed the gymnasium with distinction and entered university at fifteen for philosophy.

His father's early death forced Seidl to tutor himself and his mother, so he swapped law for teaching, qualified in 1827, and taught at Cilli's state gymnasium from 1829. False death notices praising him drew official notice. After eleven happy years he returned to Vienna as keeper of the imperial medal cabinet, later book censor to 1848, Academy member, and imperial treasurer.
